test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 29 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Read the following statements and choose the correct option:**Statement 1:** The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass situated to the south of the river Narmada.**Statement 2:** The Aravalli hills form the northern boundary of the Deccan Plateau.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• Statement 1: The **Deccan Plateau** is a **triangular landmass** that lies to the **south** of the **river Narmada**. It is one of the most significant physiographic units of **India** and forms a major part of the **Peninsular Plateau**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

• Statement 2: The **Aravalli hills** are located on the **western** and **northwestern** margins of the **Peninsular Plateau**, specifically bordering the **Central Highlands**. The **northern** boundary of the **Deccan Plateau** is actually formed by the **Satpura range**, while the **Mahadev hills**, the **Kaimur hills**, and the **Maikal range** form its **eastern extensions**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• The **Deccan Plateau** is higher in the **west** and slopes gently **eastwards**. This **geographical feature** is the reason why major **rivers** like the **Godavari**, **Krishna**, and **Kaveri** flow towards the **east** and drain into the **Bay of Bengal**.

• An extension of the **Deccan Plateau** is also visible in the **northeast**, locally known as the **Meghalaya**, **Karbi-Anglong Plateau**, and **North Cachar Hills**, separated by a fault from the **Chotanagpur Plateau**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Deccan Trap** is a distinct feature of the plateau, characterized by **black soil** of **volcanic origin**. These **igneous rocks** have denuded over time to create the fertile **regur soil**, which is ideal for **cotton cultivation**.

• The **Western Ghats** (also known as **Sahyadri**) and the **Eastern Ghats** mark the western and eastern boundaries of the **Deccan Plateau** respectively. The **Western Ghats** are continuous and higher, with an average elevation of **900 to 1600 metres**.

• The **Eastern Ghats** are lower, with an average elevation of **600 metres**, and are discontinuous because they are dissected by **rivers** flowing into the **Bay of Bengal**. They stretch from the **Mahanadi Valley** to the **Nilgiris** in the **south**.

• The **Western Ghats** cause **orographic rain** as they intercept the **southwest monsoon** winds. The height of the **Western Ghats** increases progressively from **north** to **south**.

• The **Deccan Plateau** covers an area of approximately **5 lakh square kilometres** and spans across several **Indian states**, including **Maharashtra**, **Karnataka**, **Telangana**, **Andhra Pradesh**, and **Tamil Nadu**.

**Important Points__**

• **Anai Mudi** is the highest peak of the **Peninsular Plateau** and the **Western Ghats**, standing at an elevation of **2,695 metres** in the state of **Kerala**.

• **Doda Betta** is another prominent peak in the **Western Ghats** with a height of **2,637 metres**. In contrast, **Mahendragiri** is the highest peak in the **Eastern Ghats**, located in **Odisha** at **1,501 metres**.

• The **Aravalli hills** are among the **oldest fold mountains** in the world, dating back to the **Pre-Cambrian era**. They are highly **denuded** and exist as **broken hills** extending from **Gujarat** to **Delhi**.

• The **Peninsular Plateau** is one of the **oldest landmasses** on earth, formed due to the breaking and drifting of the **Gondwana land**. It consists of **broad and shallow valleys** and **rounded hills**.

• The **Central Highlands**, the other major division of the **Peninsular Plateau**, lies to the **north** of the **Narmada river** and covers a major part of the **Malwa Plateau**.
